svg.aria-label: Diagram: what an AWS Shield Advanced subscription covers and excludes, and what a Route 53 health check does to attack detection sensitivity once associated with a protection. Shield Advanced is described as a managed service that helps protect an application against external threats like DDoS attacks, volumetric bots and vulnerability exploitation attempts, with AWS noting early that the protections received can vary depending on the customer's architecture and configuration choices. On health-based detection, Shield Advanced can be configured to use a Route 53 health check for improved responsiveness and accuracy in attack detection and mitigation, and this option works with any resource type except Route 53 hosted zones. The mechanism is a dial documented in both directions, and this is the central finding of the post. When the associated health check is unhealthy, Shield Advanced requires smaller deviations to alert and reports events more quickly. Conversely, when the associated health check is healthy, Shield Advanced requires larger deviations to alert. Associating a health check therefore does not only add sensitivity when things are bad, it removes sensitivity when the check reports fine, so a shallow check such as an HTTP 200 from a path returning a static response keeps reporting healthy while the application behind it is struggling and actively raises the threshold Shield must cross before alerting. AWS states the condition for benefit strictly: the customer will benefit most if the health check only reports healthy when the application is running within acceptable parameters and only reports unhealthy when it is not. AWS also states that Shield Advanced does not automatically manage health checks, that the customer is responsible for defining and maintaining health checks that accurately report application health, that the health check must report healthy at the moment it is associated with the protection, and that the health check must be relevant to the health of the protected resource. The first of those is an ordering constraint that can break infrastructure-as-code runs which create the health check and the association in a single pass, because a newly created check has not yet reported healthy. A second dependency is carried in a note: health checks are required for Shield Response Team proactive engagement support, meaning the response team contacting the customer rather than the customer raising a case, so the health check is a prerequisite for a headline benefit rather than an optimisation. By resource class, health-based detection improves accuracy of network and transport layer event detection and mitigation for Network Load Balancers, Elastic IP addresses and Global Accelerator standard accelerators, where Shield Advanced can provide mitigations for smaller attacks and faster mitigation even when traffic is within the application's capacity, and during unhealthy periods can place mitigations even more quickly and at lower thresholds. For application layer resources, namely CloudFront distributions and Application Load Balancers, web request flood detection alerts fire when there is a statistically significant deviation in traffic volume combined with significant changes in traffic patterns based on request characteristics. On subscription economics, the subscription covers standard AWS WAF fees for protected resources, namely the cost per protection pack or web ACL, the cost per rule, and the base price per million requests for web request inspection, bounded at up to 1,500 web ACL capacity units and up to the default body size, and it includes access to the Layer 7 Anti-DDoS Amazon Managed Rule group. Enabling automatic application layer DDoS mitigation adds a rule group consuming 150 web ACL capacity units which count against that same allowance, so the automatic mitigation consumes one tenth of the covered capacity before any customer rule, and exceeding 1,500 units does not fail but moves the web ACL into non-standard costs that the subscription explicitly does not cover. Other named non-standard costs are Bot Control, the CAPTCHA rule action, and inspecting the request body beyond the default body size, and the subscription also does not cover AWS WAF use for resources not protected by Shield Advanced, which means a web ACL serving a mix of protected and unprotected resources leaves the unprotected ones' WAF costs with the customer. The subscription includes up to 50 billion requests to protected AWS WAF resources in a calendar month, with requests beyond that billed separately. On billing structure, for accounts in an AWS Organizations organization AWS bills Shield Advanced subscriptions against the payer account regardless of whether the payer account itself is subscribed, and when multiple accounts in the same consolidated billing family are subscribed one subscription price covers all of them provided the organization owns all the accounts and their resources, while customers running more than one organization must contact their account manager or AWS support and request a fee waiver for all but one organization, which is a conversation rather than a setting.
svg.title: The Route 53 health check is a sensitivity dial, and it works in both directions
svg.text: A healthy health check makes Shield look less hard.
AWS Shield Advanced — health-based detection, and where the subscription stops.
AWS documents both ends of the dial. Most people read one.
health check UNHEALTHY → “Shield Advanced requires smaller deviations to alert and it reports events more quickly”
health check HEALTHY → “Conversely… Shield Advanced requires larger deviations to alert”
So a shallow check — HTTP 200 from a static path — does not merely fail to help. It raises the bar.
“benefit the most… if the health check only reports healthy when your application is running within acceptable parameters”
And it gates the thing you bought
“Health checks are required for Shield Response
Team (SRT) proactive engagement support.”
No check → no phone call. And “Shield Advanced doesn’t
Three requirements — one breaks your pipeline
· “must report healthy when you associate it”
· “must be relevant to the health of your… resource”
Create → wait for healthy → associate. One IaC pass fails.
automatically manage your health checks.”
The protection you switch on spends a tenth of the allowance that pays for it
Subscription covers standard WAF — per web ACL, per rule, per million requests — “up to 1,500 WCUs”
Automatic L7 mitigation “adds a rule group… that uses 150 web ACL capacity units” which “count against” it
Crossing 1,500 does not fail. It moves you into costs the subscription names as not covered.
Covered
· cost per protection pack (web ACL)
· cost per rule
· base price per million requests, to 1,500 WCUs
· inspection to the default body size
· Layer 7 Anti-DDoS Managed Rule group
· up to 50 billion requests per calendar month
Not covered
· WAF for resources you do NOT protect with Shield
· Bot Control · the CAPTCHA rule action
· web ACLs using more than 1,500 WCUs
· body inspection beyond the default size
A web ACL on 12 load balancers with 4 protected is not a
covered ACL with 8 extras. The other 8 are yours.
What the dial buys, by layer
L3/L4 — NLB, Elastic IPs, Global Accelerator: mitigations for “smaller attacks” and faster, “even when traffic is
within the application’s capacity” · L7 — CloudFront, ALB: alerts on deviation in volume and pattern
Billing is organisation-shaped: charged “against the payer account… regardless of whether the payer account itself is subscribed”,
and one price covers every subscribed account in the same consolidated billing family.
Several organisations? The consolidation is a request to your account team, not a setting: “request a fee waiver… for all but one”.
